## Scope

Data preparation turns observations into features that a model can consume reliably. The exam often tests whether a proposed workflow preserves the meaning of those features when data moves between training and prediction. Start by identifying the unit of observation and the target being predicted. A transaction, a customer, and a daily aggregate require different splits and different safeguards. Choose the evaluation boundary before fitting preprocessing statistics. Otherwise information from the evaluation population can influence transformations used during training. The resulting score may look better than the performance users actually experience. This chapter uses q_000000000001 as a prompt to examine consistency between environments. The question is evidence of an exam concept, while the technical reasoning comes from service behavior and documented design constraints. Prioritize a repeatable preparation workflow over a change that only alters model execution frequency. A regular retraining schedule cannot repair a feature definition that means different things in two environments.

A useful review also checks the assumptions behind the decision. Consider whether the input represents a single event or an accumulated history, whether the transformation needs population statistics, and whether prediction must finish within a fixed response budget. Explain the selected mechanism using those constraints. If a constraint changes, revisit the choice rather than treating a familiar service as a universal answer.

For each proposed workflow, trace a representative record from collection through preparation and prediction. Identify every place a value can change and every place a fitted parameter is loaded. Confirm that records arrive with the same units, schema, and category definitions. Then identify who deploys updates and how a rollback restores compatible artifacts. This exercise exposes mismatches that a high level architecture description can hide. A correct design includes a way to observe those mismatches and investigate their cause.

## Key concepts

A transformation graph records how raw fields become model inputs. TensorFlow Transform can analyze a training dataset to calculate constants such as means, vocabulary mappings, and normalization factors. Those constants belong to the training run. Apply the resulting graph when preparing evaluation records and when serving predictions. This keeps feature computation aligned across environments. A hand maintained preprocessing function can be sufficient for simple transformations, provided the same implementation and configuration run everywhere. Its limitation is the operational burden of distributing compatible code and dependencies. The closest alternative to a saved transformation graph is a separately maintained preprocessing service. That approach can centralize logic but adds network calls and another service to deploy. Pick it only when its operational characteristics fit the latency and reliability requirements. BigQuery provides SQL operations for exploring tabular data and constructing aggregate features. Consider query cost, point in time correctness, and ownership of transformation definitions before selecting a workflow.

## Decision table

Use the scenario cue to choose the mechanism that directly fixes the failure. When training and production calculate different category indexes, choose a shared vocabulary mapping because an identical category must refer to the same input position. When numerical normalization differs, export statistics fitted on training data and apply them consistently because evaluation and serving should use the same reference distribution. When feature values include information unavailable at prediction time, repair the temporal join because a model cannot depend on future observations. When a daily data pipeline silently drops records, add data validation and monitoring because a preprocessing graph alone cannot detect every upstream delivery failure. When a requirement concerns lower inference latency, measure where time is spent before changing batch size. The choice must follow the stated constraint. A technique that improves throughput might worsen response time for individual requests. Separate correctness problems from performance problems so that the selected service solves the issue described.

## Traps

A common mistake is treating every difference between training and production as model drift. Drift describes a distribution change, while inconsistent feature computation is an implementation problem. Another mistake is fitting vocabulary or scaling statistics on the entire dataset before splitting it. That lets the preparation stage learn about evaluation examples. Even without explicit target labels, this can make the evaluation boundary misleading. Also distinguish missing data from a meaningful zero. Imputing every missing measurement with zero can create a false signal when zero is a valid observed value. Record a missingness indicator when the absence itself matters, and check whether the same treatment can run during serving. Avoid choosing a large platform merely because it appears in the scenario. A small deterministic transformation might need only shared code and versioned configuration. Conversely, an interactive notebook alone does not provide the scheduling, validation, deployment controls, and recovery behavior required for a production preparation pipeline.
